title: SHRED: Self-Play for Heterogeneous Road-Users without Expert Demonstrations
abstract: arXiv:2610.20866v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Realistic traffic simulation and autonomous planning both depend on modeling interactions among heterogeneous road users whose dynamics, constraints, and behaviors differ fundamentally. Existing approaches predominantly learn realistic interaction behavior from large-scale human driving demonstrations. In this work, we ask whether such behavior can instead emerge purely through self-play. We present SHRED, a framework that jointly trains vehicles, pedestrians, and cyclists through large-scale heterogeneous self-play from random initialization, without demonstrations or logged-trajectory replay. SHRED combines type-specific dynamics and objectives with procedural scenario generation and per-agent randomization, allowing diverse behaviors to emerge through closed-loop interaction. On the Waymo Open Sim Agents Challenge (WOSAC), SHRED jointly controls all three road-user types and outperforms both the closest demonstration-free self-play

translated_title: SHRED：无需专家演示的异构道路使用者自我博弈方法
translated_abstract: 现实的交通仿真与自动驾驶规划都依赖于对异构道路使用者之间交互的建模，而这些道路使用者在动力学特性、约束条件和行为模式上存在根本差异。现有方法主要从大规模人类驾驶演示数据中学习真实的交互行为。在本工作中，我们探讨这种交互行为是否能够纯粹通过自我博弈自然涌现。我们提出了SHRED，这是一个从随机初始化开始、通过大规模异构自我博弈联合训练车辆、行人和骑行者的框架，无需演示数据或记录轨迹回放。SHRED将特定类型的动力学模型与目标相结合，并采用程序化场景生成和逐智能体随机化，使多样化的行为能够在闭环交互中自然涌现。在Waymo开放仿真智能体挑战赛（WOSAC）上，SHRED联合控制全部三类道路使用者，并优于最接近的无演示自我博弈方法
tldr: SHRED提出了一个无需专家演示的异构自我博弈框架，从随机初始化出发联合训练车辆、行人和骑行者三类道路使用者，使逼真的交互行为在闭环自博弈中自然涌现，并在WOSAC基准上超越现有无演示自我博弈方法。
